newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dollar level corrects undervaluation - De Silguy.
newsitem.headline: Dollar level corrects undervaluation - De Silguy.

text.p: The European Union's Economic Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault De Silguy said on Wednesday that the dollar's current level corrected its undervaluation.
"I think the dollar's current level corrects an undervaluation of this currency," De Silguy told RTL radio.
"The current (foreign exchange) levels better reflect the relative value of the economies on either side of the Atlantic," he said.

"If you look at the fundamentals, particularly in terms of job-creation, it's clear the U.S. economic situation is better than Europe's," De Silguy said in an interview, in which he also exhorted France to pursue its deficit-reduction efforts.
He said the dollar's rise would benefit Europe, as would the launch of a single European currency.
He said policies undertaken in Europe, France in particular, were also beginning to show positive results.
The new French government last week announced plans to reduce the budget deficit to help the country meet the criteria for monetary union.
De Silguy last week said he was encouraged by the plan.
